extracted.intended_audience: readers, students, and scholars of 19th-century literature (general readers of classic novels)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative points for composing or assessing realist novels—especially in portraying generational conflict, social types, and the balance of ideas and human character. Emphasises characterization, thematic clarity, and avoidance of didacticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character as embodiment of an idea made fully human
rubrics_metrics.description: Turgenev 'drew a character, Bazarov, who served to express what he taught us to call Nihilism, and made a movement into a man.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a character represents a social or ideological position, the writer should still 'make a movement into a man'—turn abstract ideas into a rounded, human individual rather than a mere mouthpiece or cold travesty. Avoid letting ideological function override humanity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Represent social types with 'sense of fitness' and care
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The Petrovitchs... were intended... to breathe "feebleness, nonchalance, narrowness of mind." His sense of fitness made him paint with extreme care these choice representatives of their class.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When portraying class-types or representative figures, attend to an appropriate 'sense of fitness': craft details and traits carefully so the type is convincing and internally consistent rather than caricatured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid tract‑novel didacticism
rubrics_metrics.description: 'But we should be wrong if we mistook its clear pervading realities for those of a tract-novel, or a document of any one particular generation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not reduce a novel to a piece of propaganda or a single‑purpose document. Even with clear themes, aim for artistic complexity and multiple dimensions rather than one-sided didacticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sympathetic understanding of multiple perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Turgenev's 'sympathetic power... instinctive understanding of them both' (the two generations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give sympathetic, nuanced portrayals to opposing sides (e.g., old and young). Empathic insight into each perspective deepens thematic tension and avoids simplistic moralising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust the moment to the permanent
rubrics_metrics.description: 'An artist who was for ever adjusting the moment to the permanent in art.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose scenes that both capture immediate, concrete moments and resonate with larger, enduring truths—craft should link transient action to lasting significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depict human foibles, pride, prejudices, and comic/tragic susceptibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: 'He loved the play of human nature, knew how to reckon with its foibles, its pride, habitual prejudices, and all tragic and comic susceptibilities.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portray characters' weaknesses and contradictions (vanity, prejudice, comic quirks, tragic flaws) with fidelity; such nuance yields richer, more believable people and tonal variety (comic and tragic).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use protagonists to express movements while humanizing them
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Bazarov... a protagonist of the revolt against the old order and the protective habit of age.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a protagonist embodies social revolt or large movements, ensure the depiction humanizes them—show internal motivations, contradictions, and personal qualities beyond the movement they represent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ literary parallels and archetypes judiciously
rubrics_metrics.description: Turgenev allows parallels (e.g., Don Quixote, Hamlet) and even compared 'the deeper essentials of Hamlet and Quixote.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawing on archetypes or canonical parallels can enrich meaning and position a work in conversation with literary tradition, but use such parallels to illuminate characters/themes rather than to substitute for original characterization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present ideological positions with craft and nuance (avoid crude delivery)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Bazarov's ideas on art, which in truth are apt to be more crudely delivered than the rest of that iconoclast's destructive opinions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When conveying characters' doctrines or theories, render them with attention to rhetorical effect and subtlety; crude exposition weakens credibility and artistic impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write with historical insight and anticipation
rubrics_metrics.description: 'History in the large has terribly and irresistibly confirmed the history in little that Turgenev drew, with a sure instinct, for the potential anticipations of his saga.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective realist fiction may capture social trends or tensions with a prescient quality—observe and dramatise particulars that reflect broader historical or social currents, enabling the work to resonate beyond its immediate setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain an unromantic (restrained) tonal stance where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduction calls the book 'masterly unromantic novel.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A restrained, unromantic tone can serve realism by avoiding sentimental embellishment; choose tone deliberately to suit subject-matter and to preserve clarity of depiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the central theme clear (title reflecting thematic focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'It is as its title declares in a sense another fable of the inevitable coil and recoil of the two generations.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure thematic focus is coherently signalled—titles and framing can (and should) echo the central conflict or motif so readers grasp the work's organizing idea without reducing complexity.
